exposure: head lifting method during caesarean section
cohort: The study included 88 women experiencing obstructed labour during caesarean section, randomly divided into two groups.
finding: Reversed breech extraction method was associated with significantly lower maternal and fetal risks compared to the head lifting method during caesarean section.
mod_finding: Reversed breech extraction method during caesarean section resulted in significantly lower uterine artery injury, uterine extension, blood transfusion, operation time, and better fetal outcomes (birth weight, APGAR scores, NICU admission) compared to the head lifting method.
